cohort: The study included liveborn deliveries undergoing a trial of labor from 34 weeks 0 days to 42 weeks 6 days to patients aged 16-50 years.
finding: The primary finding was a national decline in operative vaginal delivery, with significantly greater declines in forceps-assisted vaginal delivery, and an increasing rate of obstetric anal sphincter injuries among forceps-assisted vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Operative vaginal delivery rates decreased significantly from 4.6% to 4.1% (FAVD from 0.8% to 0.6%, VAVD from 3.8% to 3.4%), and there was a higher likelihood of OASIS in FAVD (aOR 9.50) and VAVD (aOR 3.90) compared to spontaneous vaginal birth, with OASIS rates among FAVD increasing from 9.3% in 2016 to 14.0% in 2023.
